subtopics: Using dictionaries to organize application data
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of vbscript collections and dictionaries in a Classic ASP application.
Identify and describe at least two syllabus subtopics: Introduction to collections and The Scripting.Dictionary object.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study vbscript collections and dictionaries as part of Classic ASP development and legacy maintenance. The lesson follows the attached ASP curriculum topic 29 and uses the syllabus subtopics as the coverage checklist.
content.why_it_matters: VBScript Collections and Dictionaries matters because Classic ASP behavior crosses a server-side scripting engine, IIS configuration, request/response boundaries, and often COM or ADO dependencies. A small, explicit test helps distinguish intended behavior from runtime-specific behavior.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Intermediate VBScript code benefits from predictable object lifetime, focused error handling, and small reusable procedures. For 'VBScript Collections and Dictionaries', choose the simplest construct that matches the requirement, document any COM dependency, and avoid suppressing errors across unrelated statements. A legacy script can be improved without changing externally visible behavior by adding focused checks first.

content_blocks.title: Syllabus coverage
content_blocks.text: The lesson explicitly covers: Introduction to collections; The Scripting.Dictionary object; Keys and values; Adding and removing entries; Checking whether a key exists; Iterating through dictionary entries; Using dictionaries to organize application data. Treat these subtopics as connected requirements. For each one, be able to define the concept, identify where it appears in a Classic ASP application, and name one test or diagnostic that would verify it.

content_blocks.title: Inspectable example: VBScript Collections and Dictionaries
content_blocks.code:
<%
Dim settings
Set settings = Server.CreateObject("Scripting.Dictionary")
settings.Add "theme", "light"
If settings.Exists("theme") Then Response.Write settings("theme")
Set settings = Nothing
%>
content_blocks.run_instructions: Treat dictionary keys as part of a small contract; check existence before reading optional keys. content_blocks.text: 1. Start with a minimal local example of vbscript collections and dictionaries. 2. Trace its inputs, state changes, dependencies, and output. 3. Test a normal case, a missing/malformed case, and one permission/provider/runtime failure. 4. Write down the exact expected and observed result before changing another variable.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating legacy runtime behavior as universal.
common_mistakes.why: IIS versions, Windows lifecycle, COM registration/bitness, and ADO providers can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Write down the actual server/provider versions and validate on a disposable test site.

common_mistakes.why: Empty input, missing records, expired sessions, permissions, timeouts, and malformed data reveal different failure modes.
common_mistakes.fix: Add normal, negative, and boundary cases with expected outcomes.

common_mistakes.why: Detailed errors can reveal paths, SQL text, configuration, and component information.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep diagnostics in restricted server-side logs and return a generic message with a reference ID.
